purpose: Narrow novelty/interpretation check after paired-format result; not a fresh hypothesis search or replication claim.

sources.title: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-shot Performance of Language Models
sources.observed_by_authors: Answer priors and prompt format/order affect classification accuracy; contextual calibration can reduce instability.
sources.our_relation: General answer-token bias is established prior work. Our narrower result is the interaction of a scripted compliance claim and verdict coding in an exact-oracle safety-monitor task. We did not test their contextual-calibration procedure.

sources.title: SLEIGHT-Bench: Finding Blind Spots in AI Monitors
sources.observed_by_authors: Synthetic attack transcripts expose monitoring blind spots; paired benign variants calibrate low-FPR thresholds. Targeted prompts can improve one category while worsening another.
sources.our_relation: Our study isolates scripted comment and output-format changes on fully specified synthetic permission traces. It tests a smaller, simpler monitor and different threat model; not a SLEIGHT benchmark replication. Lower false alarms in semantic formats do not establish global monitor robustness.

sources.title: Safety Monitors Mostly Catch What the Model Already Refuses
sources.observed_by_authors: Abstract reports lower recall on harmful requests the target actually answers, despite high aggregateAUROC, and attributes linked model/monitor failures to explicitness cues.
sources.our_relation: Supports examining behavior-conditioned detection and cue dependence in Exp2, rather than treating aggregate predictive accuracy as safety assurance. Preprint findings not independently reproduced here.
